script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the book’s leader and point total are unknown and the script is inferred from weeks 2–4 form only. Base case is a competitive game with both workhorse backs involved: Jonathan Taylor 67 carries/255 yards (about 22.3 carries, 3.81 YPC) and Jaylen Warren 45/263 (15 carries, 5.84 YPC). IND’s pass tree stays Downs-led (24 targets, 165 yards, 243 air) with Tyler Warren on short targets (22/117/36 air); PIT throws downfield to DK Metcalf (23/173/290 air) and Roman Wilson (18/162/242 air) and still dumps to Warren (14 targets, 116 yards, -9 air). IND’s rush defense is the softer front (4.97 YPC, 12 runs of 10+ vs PIT’s 4.56 YPC and 11 runs of 10+), so PIT can run without abandoning the pass.
script.flip1: IND leads late: PIT abandons the run, Warren’s carries die the way a trailing back’s rushing line dies, and PIT target volume rises toward Wilson, Metcalf, Freiermuth and Warren’s checkdowns. Taylor’s rush attempts can stall if IND clocks out.
script.flip2: PIT leads big, or an unknown weather/slog game cuts plays: PIT runs Warren late and Roman Wilson’s routes stall; deep air-yard overs (Wilson, Metcalf, Downs) are the first to miss. Live weather is not in the pack, so this flip is untestable before kickoff.

Downs (24 targets, 243 air) would attack PIT’s depleted secondary (Elliott out, Dean out, Ramsey Q), but PIT’s middle — the likely slot area — is PIT’s best zone at 7.15 YPA, and Downs’ line is not short of his production.

pre_mortem: It’s Monday and both lost. Warren’s 20.5 died because IND did not blitz (20%, Key out), Rodgers never had to dump off, and a linebacker replacement sat on the flat, turning 4.7 targets into two catches for 12 yards — the 27-yard floor was opponent-driven, not a right. Wilson’s 41 died because the 60 and 74 were single explosives, Pittman’s 9 low-value targets did not become a full route package, and PIT leaned on Warren’s 5.84 YPC against a 4.97 rush defense and took the vertical shots away. That counter is real for Wilson (why he stays a lean, not a strong) and is not stronger than Warren’s four-game floor plus the Carlies hole, so Warren stays and Wilson is not dropped.
slip_story: One PIT skill-player story, not a total and not an IND stack: IND’s front seven is short Key and Carlies, so Warren’s checkdown yards and Wilson’s downfield yards can hit together in a competitive game where PIT still throws. Do not add Warren rush or rush+rec (one market per player; rush needs the lead script that can kill Wilson). Do not pair with a game under or with Taylor rush-clock legs, which need a different leader. Downs was considered for the PIT-secondary injuries and passed because 55.5 equals his L3 average after a 16-yard week 4 and PIT’s middle is their best zone (7.15 YPA).
